title: Слово о пълку Игоревѣ
part: II — The two days of battle
draftNote: Part II — the two days of battle: two source paragraphs of the 1800 edition, the first day's rout and plunder of the Polovtsian camp, the apostrophe to Oleg's 'brave nest' and the fleeing khans Gzak and Konchak, then (new paragraph) the ominous dawn of the second day (storm-clouds 'meaning to cover the four suns'), the refrain «O Russian land» returning darkened, the Polovtsian encirclement, and the long apostrophe to Vsevolod, 'Yar Tur.'
source: Text: editio princeps — «Ироическая пѣснь о походѣ на половцовъ удѣльнаго князя Новагорода-Сѣверскаго Игоря Святославича», ed. A. I. Musin-Pushkin, Moscow, 1800 (public domain); via Russian Wikisource. 1800 orthography preserved. Prose sense-units at the edition's punctuation (no imposed verse lineation). Transliteration: scholarly Slavist romanization (ž š č c x; ě = ѣ; ŭ / ĭ = ъ / ь). Pronunciation: reconstructed late-12th-c. Old East Slavic (see slovo-audio doc); ж/ш/ц read hard by convention. Translations made fresh from the 1800 original.
about: The battle proper, told in two days. On the first day the Rus' rout the Polovtsian camp and plunder it — gold, silks, captive women, enough finery to corduroy roads over the marshes — while the poet turns, in a sudden apostrophe, to Igor's own house, 'Oleg's brave nest,' now far from home; the historical khans Gzak and Konchak are named fleeing toward the Don. At dawn on the second day the omens turn openly hostile — bloody skies, black storm-clouds 'meaning to cover the four suns,' thunder and a rain of arrows foretold at the river Kayala — and the poem's great refrain returns inverted: no longer safely 'beyond the hill,' the Russian land now stands exposed. The Polovtsians close in from every side, the Rus' regiments give ground behind a wall of crimson shields, and the movement ends on a long, celebrated apostrophe to Igor's brother Vsevolod, 'Yar Tur,' fighting on almost single-handed. As throughout, the poem survives only in this 1800 edition — the medieval copy burned in 1812 — and several passages here, flagged in the notes, are among its most debated 'dark places.'

sentences.t: Съ заранія въ пяткъ потопташа поганыя плъкы Половецкыя; и рассушясь стрѣлами по полю, помчаша красныя дѣвкы Половецкыя, а съ ними злато, и паволокы, и драгыя оксамиты;
sentences.tr: Sŭ zaranija vŭ pjatkŭ potoptaša poganyja plŭky Poloveckyja; i rassušjasĭ strělami po polju, pomčaša krasnyja děvky Poloveckyja, a sŭ nimi zlato, i pavoloky, i dragyja oksamity;
sentences.l: From early morning, on Friday, [they] trampled down the pagan Polovtsian troops; and having scattered with arrows across the field, [they] drove off the fair Polovtsian maidens, and with them gold, and silk cloths, and precious samite;
sentences.i: From early morning on that Friday, they trampled down the pagan Polovtsian regiments; scattering with their arrows across the field, they carried off the fair Polovtsian girls — and with them gold, and silken cloths, and costly samite —
sentences.n: The subject (the Rus' warriors) is left unstated, continuing straight on from part 1. потопташа and помчаша are aorists, 3pl, 'they trampled' / 'they drove off, carried away.' рассушясь is a reflexive past participle, 'having scattered themselves' — the same kind of form as part 1's наплънився. Battle day one is dated precisely: «въ пяткъ», 'on a Friday.' оксамиты = 'samite,' a costly silk-velvet fabric of Byzantine type; паволокы likewise names fine imported silk cloth — the beginning of a plunder-catalogue.

sentences.t: орьтъмами и япончицами, и кожухы начашя мосты мостити по болотомъ и грязивымъ мѣстомъ, и всякыми узорочьи Половѣцкыми.
sentences.tr: Orĭtŭmami i japončicami, i kožuxy načašja mosty mostiti po bolotomŭ i grjazivymŭ městomŭ, i vsjakymi uzoročĭi Polověckymi.
sentences.l: with horse-rugs and cloaks, and with fur coats [they] began to bridge bridges over the swamps and the muddy places, and with all kinds of Polovtsian finery.
sentences.i: with saddle-rugs and cloaks and fur coats they began laying causeways over the marshes and the miry ground — and with every sort of Polovtsian finery besides.
sentences.n: орьтъмами, япончицами, кожухы (all instrumental) are the very plunder that becomes the roadbed — орьтъма, a rare word usually taken for a horsecloth or rug; япончица, a diminutive of the cloak-word япончь (from a Turkic loan). «мосты мостити», literally 'to bridge bridges,' is the poem's cognate-object figure for corduroying a path. начашя is an aorist 3pl, 'they began.' узорочьи (instr. pl.) = costly trinkets, finery; the catalogue of plunder begun in the previous unit closes here.

sentences.t: Чрьленъ стягъ, бѣла хорюговь, чрьлена чолка, сребрено стружіе храброму Святьславличю. Дремлетъ въ полѣ Ольгово хороброе гнѣздо далече залетѣло;
sentences.tr: Črĭlenŭ stjagŭ, běla xorjugovĭ, črĭlena čolka, srebreno stružie xrabromu Svjatĭslavličju. Dremletŭ vŭ polě Olĭgovo xorobroe gnězdo daleče zaletělo;
sentences.l: A crimson banner, a white gonfalon, a crimson horsetail-standard, a silver-clad spear-staff — to the brave son of Svyatoslav. Oleg's brave nest slumbers in the field, having flown far away;
sentences.i: A crimson banner, a white gonfalon, a crimson horsetail-standard, a silver-shod standard-staff — these belong to the brave son of Svyatoslav. Out in the field, Oleg's bold nest lies dozing, gone far from its home ground;
sentences.n: A run of verbless clauses inventories the princely war-standards: banner, gonfalon, чолка (literally 'tuft, forelock,' usually read as a horsetail-standard of the eastern steppe type), and стружіе, a spear- or standard-staff — all in the Rus' color crimson, with white. храброму Святьславличю (dat. sg.), 'to the brave son of Svyatoslav,' names their owner. «Ольгово хороброе гнѣздо», 'Oleg's brave nest,' figures Igor's line as descendants of Oleg Svyatoslavich, the strife-sowing prince recalled again in part 1 and later in the poem — here pictured as a nest that has flown far from its home ground. залетѣло is a past tense, 3sg neut.

sentences.t: небылонъ обидѣ порождено, ни соколу, ни кречету, ни тебѣ чръный воронъ, поганый Половчине.
sentences.tr: Nebylonŭ obidě poroždeno, ni sokolu, ni krečetu, ni tebě črŭnyj voronŭ, poganyj Polovčine.
sentences.l: [it] was not born to offense, neither to falcon, nor to gyrfalcon, nor to you, black raven, pagan Polovtsian.
sentences.i: born, it was not, to be anyone's prey — not the falcon's, not the gyrfalcon's, nor yours, black raven, pagan son of the steppe.
sentences.n: One of the poem's genuine dark places: «небылонъ обидѣ порождено» is corrupt or at least ungrammatical as printed, and no single reading commands agreement — we keep the 1800 letters exactly and translate only approximately. The general sense usually taken is that Oleg's noble 'nest' was never born to suffer insult — not from the falcon or the gyrfalcon (noble hunting birds, standing for worthy rivals), and certainly not from the raven, a carrion-bird here standing in contemptuously for the Polovtsian foe, addressed directly as «чръный воронъ» and «поганый Половчине». «Половчине» is a true vocative (-инъ stems like Половчинъ form the vocative singular in -ине, as in господине from господинъ); «чръный воронъ» stays in the nominative form used for address, as some nouns do.

sentences.t: Гзакъ бѣжитъ сѣрымъ влъкомъ; Кончакъ ему слѣдъ править къ Дону великому.
sentences.tr: Gzakŭ běžitŭ sěrymŭ vlŭkomŭ; Končakŭ jemu slědŭ pravitĭ kŭ Donu velikomu.
sentences.l: Gzak flees as a grey wolf; Konchak directs the path for him toward the great Don.
sentences.i: Gzak flees like a grey wolf, while Konchak guides the way for him toward the great Don.
sentences.n: Gzak (Гзакъ) and Konchak (Кончакъ) are historical Polovtsian khans named in the Hypatian Chronicle's account of the 1185 campaign — Konchak the senior khan, Gzak commanding a separate force. сѣрымъ влъкомъ (instr. sg.), 'as a grey wolf,' is the same wolf-simile met of the Rus' warriors in part 1, now turned onto the fleeing enemy. править here means 'to set straight, to direct' the path, not 'to rule.'

sentences.t: Другаго дни велми рано кровавыя зори свѣтъ повѣдаютъ; чръныя тучя съморя идутъ, хотятъ прикрыти д̃ солнца:
sentences.tr: Drugago dni velmi rano krovavyja zori světŭ povědajutŭ; črŭnyja tučja sŭmorja idutŭ, xotjatŭ prikryti d̃ solnca:
sentences.l: Of the next day, very early, bloody dawns proclaim the light; black storm-clouds move up from the sea, meaning to shroud the four suns:
sentences.i: Early on the next day, bloody dawns herald the light, while black clouds sweep in off the sea to blot out the four suns:
sentences.n: «Другаго дни» (gen. sg.) is a genitive of time, 'on the next day' — the second, disastrous day of battle opens. д̃ is a letter under a titlo, here the numeral value 4 ('четыре,' 'four'); «прикрыти д̃ солнца», 'to cover the four suns,' is almost always read as the four Rus' commanders present on the campaign, though which four exactly is not stated by the poem and remains debated — we keep that uncertainty rather than naming a fixed list.

sentences.t: а въ нихъ трепещуть синіи млъніи, быти грому великому, итти дождю стрѣлами съ Дону великаго:
sentences.tr: A vŭ nixŭ trepeščutĭ sinii mlŭnii, byti gromu velikomu, itti doždju strělami sŭ Donu velikago:
sentences.l: and in them tremble blue lightnings — there is to be great thunder, there is to come a rain of arrows from the great Don:
sentences.i: and within them blue lightnings flicker — great thunder is coming, a rain of arrows is coming up from the great Don:
sentences.n: «быти грому великому» and «итти дождю» are the infinitive-plus-dative 'is-to-be' construction: an impersonal future or necessity built from the infinitives быти/итти with a dative logical subject (грому, дождю) rather than a normal personal verb — literally 'to great thunder [there] is to be,' 'to rain [there] is to come.' стрѣлами (instr. pl.) turns the coming rain into a rain 'of arrows,' the coming Polovtsian arrow-fire figured as a storm.

sentences.t: ту ся копіемъ приламати, ту ся саблямъ потручяти о шеломы Половецкыя, на рѣцѣ на Каялѣ, у Дону великаго.
sentences.tr: Tu sja kopiemŭ prilamati, tu sja sabljamŭ potručjati o šelomy Poloveckyja, na rěcě na Kajalě, u Donu velikago.
sentences.l: here it is for spears to be broken, here it is for sabers to be shattered, against the Polovtsian helmets — on the river, on the Kayala, by the great Don.
sentences.i: here spears will break, here sabers will shatter against Polovtsian helms — on the river Kayala, by the great Don.
sentences.n: The enclitic reflexive ся with an infinitive (ту ся ... приламати, ту ся ... потручяти) gives an impersonal, passive-like sense — 'is to be broken,' rather than any literal self-breaking; копіемъ and саблямъ (instr.) name the true instruments. «на рѣцѣ на Каялѣ» doubles the preposition for emphasis, an epic formula. The Kayala (Каяла), the river of the battle and the disaster, cannot be matched to any known waterway and, as elsewhere in this reading, is left unidentified. потручяти is itself a rare word, glossed here as 'to strike against, to shatter.'

sentences.t: О Руская землѣ! уже не Шеломянемъ еси.
sentences.tr: O Ruskaja zemlě! uže ne Šelomjanemŭ jesi.
sentences.l: O Russian land! already not by-the-Shelomya are you.
sentences.i: O land of Rus'! already you are no longer beyond the hill.
sentences.n: The great refrain returns from part 1, darkened. There, «уже за Шеломянемъ еси» ('already you are beyond the hill') marked the army's confident crossing of the frontier ridge outward; here the 1800 print gives «не Шеломянемъ еси» without the preposition за. Most readers take it as short for «не за Шеломянемъ», mirroring part 1's phrasing and reversing its sense — the land is no longer safely beyond the hill, but exposed. We keep the 1800 wording, missing preposition and all, rather than silently restoring it.

sentences.t: Се вѣтри, Стрибожи внуци, вѣютъ съморя стрѣлами на храбрыя плъкы Игоревы!
sentences.tr: Se větri, Striboži vnuci, vějutŭ sŭmorja strělami na xrabryja plŭky Igorevy!
sentences.l: Behold, the winds, grandsons of Stribog, blow arrows from the sea against Igor's brave regiments!
sentences.i: See how the winds, Stribog's grandsons, come sweeping arrows off the sea against Igor's brave troops!
sentences.n: Стрибогъ (Stribog) is an East Slavic wind-god named among the idols Prince Vladimir set up on a hill above Kiev, in the Primary Chronicle's account of 980 (the idols stood until the Baptism of Rus' in 988, when Vladimir had them destroyed). «Стрибожи внуци», 'Stribog's grandsons,' are the winds themselves — the same mythic-grandson figure used of Boyan as «Велесовь внуче» in part 1; the house convention keeps these epithets untranslated and glossed. Се is the presentative particle, 'behold, lo.'

sentences.t: земля тутнетъ, рѣкы мутно текуть; пороси поля прикрываютъ; стязи глаголютъ, Половци идуть отъ Дона, и отъ моря, и отъ всѣхъ странъ.
sentences.tr: Zemlja tutnetŭ, rěky mutno tekutĭ; porosi polja prikryvajutŭ; stjazi glagoljutŭ, Polovci idutĭ otŭ Dona, i otŭ morja, i otŭ vsěxŭ stranŭ.
sentences.l: the earth rumbles, the rivers flow turbidly; dust-clouds cover the fields; the banners speak: the Polovtsians come from the Don, and from the sea, and from all sides.
sentences.i: the earth booms, the rivers run murky; clouds of dust cover the plains; the standards give tongue — the Polovtsians are advancing from the Don, from the sea, from every quarter.
sentences.n: A run of short present-tense verbs (тутнетъ, текуть, прикрываютъ, глаголютъ, идуть) speeds the whole Polovtsian host converging from every direction at once. «стязи глаголютъ», 'the standards speak,' personifies the enemy banners as a kind of war-cry.

sentences.t: Рускыя плъкы отступиша. Дѣти бѣсови кликомъ поля прегородиша, а храбріи Русици преградиша чрълеными щиты.
sentences.tr: Ruskyja plŭky otstupiša. Děti běsovi klikomŭ polja pregorodiša, a xrabrii Rusici pregradiša črŭlenymi ščity.
sentences.l: The Rus' regiments withdrew. The children of demons barred the fields with a cry, but the brave men of Rus' walled [themselves] off with crimson shields.
sentences.i: The Rus' regiments fell back. The demons' children hemmed in the fields with their war-cry, but the brave sons of Rus' walled themselves off behind crimson shields.
sentences.n: отступиша, прегородиша, преградиша are all aorists, 3pl — прегородиша and преградиша are near-synonyms set side by side, the poem's characteristic doubling. «Дѣти бѣсови», 'children of demons,' is the poem's scornful epithet for the pagan Polovtsians. чрълеными щиты, 'with crimson shields,' repeats the Rus' battle-color and the shield-wall image that closed part 1.

sentences.t: Яръ туре Всеволодѣ! стоиши на борони, прыщеши на вои стрѣлами, гремлеши о шеломы мечи харалужными.
sentences.tr: Jarŭ ture Vsevolodě! stoiši na boroni, pryščeši na voi strělami, gremleši o šelomy meči xaralužnymi.
sentences.l: Furious Bull, Vsevolod! You stand in the battle-line, you shower the warriors with arrows, you thunder on helmets with swords of kharalug [steel].
sentences.i: Yar Tur Vsevolod! You hold the front of the battle, raining arrows on the foe, ringing their helmets with your blades of tempered steel.
sentences.n: «Яръ туре Всеволодѣ», 'Furious Bull, Vsevolod' (kept untranslated as 'Yar Tur' in `i`, as part 1 keeps 'Buy Tur'), echoes part 1's «Буй Туръ Всеволодъ» with a different adjective (яръ 'fierce, furious' beside буй 'wild'), now addressed directly in the vocative. Three 2sg present verbs (стоиши, прыщеши, гремлеши) paint him fighting almost single-handed. харалужными, 'of kharalug [steel],' names a legendary, especially hard tempered steel used several times in the poem for the finest blades; its exact linguistic origin is debated, but it consistently marks the very best weapons.

sentences.t: Камо Туръ поскочяше, своимъ златымъ шеломомъ посвѣчивая, тамо лежатъ поганыя головы Половецкыя;
sentences.tr: Kamo Turŭ poskočjaše, svoimŭ zlatymŭ šelomomŭ posvěčivaja, tamo ležatŭ poganyja golovy Poloveckyja;
sentences.l: Wherever the Bull kept charging, glinting with his own golden helmet, there lie the pagan Polovtsian heads;
sentences.i: Wherever the Bull drove forward, his golden helmet ablaze, there the pagan Polovtsian heads lie fallen;
sentences.n: поскочяше has imperfect morphology, 'kept charging, would charge' — a habitual sense fitting 'wherever [he] charged.' посвѣчивая is a present active participle, 'flashing, gleaming,' picturing Vsevolod's helmet as he moves. Туръ stands alone here as his name-title, continuing the direct address from the previous unit.

sentences.t: поскепаны саблями калеными шеломы Оварьскыя отъ тебе Яръ Туре Всеволоде.
sentences.tr: Poskepany sabljami kalenymi šelomy Ovarĭskyja otŭ tebe Jarŭ Ture Vsevolode.
sentences.l: hewn apart by tempered sabers are the Avar helmets, by you, Furious Bull, Vsevolod.
sentences.i: the very helmets of the Avars lie hewn apart by tempered sabers — struck down by you, Yar Tur Vsevolod.
sentences.n: поскепаны (past passive participle, nom. pl.) 'split, hacked apart'; калеными (instr. pl.), 'tempered [in fire].' Оварьскыя, 'of the Avars' — the early medieval steppe people whose eventual ruin the Primary Chronicle itself recalls proverbially ('погибоша аки Обре,' 'they perished like the Avars'); their helmets stand here, hyperbolically, for the toughest armor imaginable, split by Vsevolod's blows. The unit, and the movement, close as they opened — on a direct vocative address to him.

glossary.заранія: заранье — early morning (gen. sg., 'from early morning')
glossary.въ: въ — on, in (prep. + acc., of time)
glossary.пяткъ: пятъкъ — Friday (acc. sg.; the fifth day, from пять 'five')
glossary.рассушясь: разсутися — having scattered, dispersed themselves (past participle, reflexive)
glossary.паволокы: паволока — silk cloths, fine fabrics (acc. pl.)
glossary.орьтъмами: орьтьма — horse-rugs, blankets (instr. pl.; rare word)
glossary.япончицами: япончица — cloaks, mantles (instr. pl.; dim. of япончь)
glossary.кожухы: кожухъ — fur coats, hides (instr. pl.; o-stem instr. pl. = acc. pl. form)
glossary.болотомъ: болото — swamps, marshes (dat. pl., 'across the swamps')
glossary.всякыми: всякый — every sort of, all kinds of (instr. pl.)
glossary.хорюговь: хорюговь — gonfalon, banner (nom. sg. fem.; = хоругвь)
glossary.святьславличю: Святьславличь — to the Svyatoslavich, son of Svyatoslav (dat. sg.; patronymic)
glossary.ольгово: Ольговъ — Oleg's (possessive adj., nom. sg. neut.); Oleg Svyatoslavich, Igor's grandfather
glossary.залетѣло: залетѣти — has flown far off (past tense, 3sg neut.)
glossary.небылонъ: — (a corrupt, uncertain reading: 'was not... born'? — a genuine dark place)
glossary.обидѣ: обида — to offense, to insult (dat. sg.)
glossary.порождено: породити — born, brought forth (past passive participle, neut. sg.)
glossary.гзакъ: Гзакъ — Gzak (nom. sg.); a historical Polovtsian khan of the 1185 campaign
glossary.кончакъ: Кончакъ — Konchak (nom. sg.); a historical Polovtsian khan of the 1185 campaign
glossary.дону: Донъ — the Don (dat./gen. sg.); the river
glossary.другаго: другый — the next, the second (gen. sg.; 'другаго дни' = 'on the next day')
glossary.съморя: съ моря — from the sea (prep. + gen., printed as one word)
glossary.д̃: (numeral 'four,' четыре — the letter д under a titlo used as a number)
glossary.быти: быти — to be (infinitive; here in the dative 'is-to-be' construction)
glossary.потручяти: потручяти — to strike against, to shatter (infinitive; rare word)
glossary.каялѣ: Каяла — the river Kayala (loc. sg.; unidentified)
glossary.руская: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (voc. sg. fem.)
glossary.землѣ: земля — O land! (voc. sg.; here without the 'за' of part 1's parallel refrain)
glossary.шеломянемъ: шеломя — the frontier hill, ridge (instr. sg.)
glossary.стрибожи: Стрибожь — Stribog's (possessive adj., nom. pl.); of the wind-god Stribog
glossary.кликомъ: кликъ — with a cry, a shout (instr. sg.)
glossary.русици: Русичь — men of Rus', sons of Rus' (nom. pl.)
glossary.борони: боронь — the defense, the battle-line (loc. sg.)
glossary.гремлеши: гремѣти — you thunder, you clang (2sg pres.)
glossary.харалужными: харалужный — of kharalug [steel], tempered (instr. pl.); a legendary hard steel
glossary.туръ: туръ — the Bull (nom. sg.; Vsevolod's epithet used as a name)
glossary.поскепаны: поскепати — split, hacked apart (past passive participle, nom. pl.)
glossary.оварьскыя: Оварьскый — Avar, of the Avars (nom. pl., adj.)
